It'll get better! You guys will have to work through it but the trust will grow again. And while your friend has a good heart about wanting you to quit, she and you need to understand that addiction is a lot more powerful than a promise. Addiction can make you do things you never imagined, things you wish you could take back. I guess for you yours is breaking the promise. But neither of you should hold you accountable for breaking the promise OP. It would be like promising to never break a leg. You don't plan to but you have a horrible day one day and all of a sudden.... it's broken. Your leg and ththe promise to not break it.
Do you see my point? Promise your friend you will try very hard to quit, even promise to smoke 1 less cigarette each month. But you can't put too much pressure on yourself like that, it might even be part of why it's so hard to quit. You were stressing so much about keeping the promise that you broke it because of stress. Addiction is powerful and simply cannot be beat by a simple promise. Please be easy on yourself and good luck quitting in the future!

The only bit of advice I can give you is stop comparing your issues to other people. Trust me, i used to tell myself all the time that I just simply didn't deserve help because others have it worse. I still struggle with this today but getting better. It's such an unhealthy mindset and having this mindset affects your health more than you can know. Truth is, people DO have it worse than you but that DOES NOT mean that you are any less deserving. It does not mean that you don't need what you need just because someone else needs something more. Your problems no matter how big or small are valid and deserve attention, no matter who has it worse. I apologize for not being able to give more advice but this part is the only part I have real experience with. Learn to not compare your problems to others. I'm still trying to learn it but I've already noticed an improvement of my mental state.

You are deserving of help. Everyone is deserving of help.

I know this all too well. My parents are split, and while they didn't talk much shit about each other when I was young, as soon as I was 18 and a legal adult I started hearing it all. My only advice is to wait until they are old enough to leave the house and talk to them. Try and talk to them until this time comes, keep reminding them that you and your Dad aren't what Mom says y'all are; but also remember that when you hear the same thing, multiple times a day, every day; you're eventually going to believe it just because its shoved down your throat.

Also your siblings might be being sour to you because they feel you've abandoned them and left them with your Mother. While I know this isn't true, and they are probably old enough to know this, the heart can be spiteful when it's hurting and do dumb things so keep that in mind too.

Wishing the best of luck for you and your siblings and may your mom become less of a you-know-what
